Subject: Q2 usage & health summary — growth handoff + burst option

Hi Tom / Hannah,

Thanks again for the run-through yesterday. I pulled together a short snapshot of Q2 usage and a couple low-friction options to avoid interrupting your product roadmap as volume ramps. Attachments: codexly_q2_token_breakdown.csv and latency-samples.pdf.

Quick highlights:
- Token consumption: ~12.4M tokens in June (up 48% vs May). The growth is concentrated in the new summarization endpoint (70% of incremental tokens).
- Unit economics: current hosted rate would imply ~22% higher monthly spend if usage continues on the same mix; with a 20% commit increase plus 50k burst credits we project a 9% net delta vs pay-as-you-go.
- Latency: 95th percentile has modestly increased (from 180ms to ~260ms) during peak windows; sample traces attached. No correctness regressions surfaced in the eval set we ran, but we saw a slight increase in truncation events for very long contexts.

Options we recommend (short list):
1) Commit increase: +20% baseline commit to lock in lower unit pricing and provide headroom for the summarization burst.
2) Burst credits: 50k token burst pool for unexpected spikes (applies before autoscaling).
3) Quantization toggle for the summarization model (Priyom and Laura can propose a safe profile that preserves ROUGE/F1 to within 1-2%).

Suggested next steps:
- Internal handoff: can Laura and Priyom validate the projected cost delta and put together a one-slide ROI for the Execs?
- External decision: Tom/Hannah, if you want to proceed we can send a one-off amendment (30-day) to add commit + burst and roll this into the July billing cycle.

Available times for a short call: Thu 7/1 10-11am PT or Fri 7/2 2pm PT.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Sean — thanks for the fast summary and the attachments. A few quick clarifying Qs before we loop in finance: 

1) The 22% higher spend forecast — is that based on current model family and token mix? If we switch to the quantized profile you mention, do those savings show up in the model unit pricing or only in latency improvements?

2) If we do the +20% commit, how quickly can that be applied / reversed? We have a customer pilot kicking off mid-July and want the ability to scale down if the pilot fizzles.

3) Can you confirm whether the burst credits are used before or after our commit? Also, how are they reported in billing? Amanda needs the line items for her ledger.

If the answers look clean we can tentatively OK the amendment; I prefer to get the ROI slide for our CFO before signatures. Meeting times: Fri 7/2 2pm PT works for me.

—Tom
Tom Alvarez
Director of ML Platforms, Codexly

Sean / team / Tom — quick take and attached: q2-econ-proposal.pdf (one-slide ROI + billing lines). Key points: 

- Validation of the projection: the 22% delta Tom references is the PAYG (no commit) projection based on the June token mix and current per-token unit prices. If Codexly moves to the +20% commit, the per-token effective price on the hot model family drops ~14% in our internal rate table, which yields the net ~9% delta I mentioned in the initial note. Numbers are in the attached slide.

- Quantization: Priyom ran an internal experiment on the summarization model (INT8-style profile). Observed outcomes: ~18% reduction in GPU cycles per token, median latency improvement of ~30ms on our fleet, and evaluation against the Codexly prompt suite showed an average ROUGE-L delta of -0.8 points (within your stated tolerance). Savings translate to lower runtime cost rather than an explicit per-token rate change — however with lower runtime cost we can justify a model variant routing that reduces billable GPU seconds on Dedicated pools. Priyom, feel free to add a sentence on rollout safety.

- Burst credits and billing: burst credits are consumed after commit is exhausted; they show as a separate line item on the monthly invoice labeled "Burst credits (one-off)" and are reconciled in the usage CSV we attach. We can make the line item more granular for your accounting team.

- Operational rollback: commits can be adjusted monthly; for an immediate scale-down we typically require a 7-day notice to align capacity pools — we can offer a provisional 7-day buffer for this pilot.

Recommendation: proceed with +20% commit + 50k burst credits for July, sign the one-off amendment (DocuSign link below) and we’ll enable the quantized model variant behind a feature flag for two weeks with automatic rollback if eval metrics degrade beyond thresholds.

DocuSign (amendment): https://www.docusign.com/overview/RDW-3749
ROI slide attached: q2-econ-proposal.pdf

Laura Bennett
